author: StaticFaultz
body:
I did state this in an earlier report, but I just want to put this out there for the community to think about it.

So anyways, the title explains my suggestion for this server/network. I have not experienced seeing an infraction message, but viewing the abundance of infractions on the infractions page, almost all of them state a phrase of sorts, like "team griefing" or "hacking: fly". Very simple statements.

I know the general whole of this part of the community that actively participate on the forums knows that these messages indicate what that player has done, but remember that Avicus is made up of a lot more than the amount presented on the forums that are mentally challenged in understanding the messages like those issued in infractions now. Because of this, I suggest that infraction messages be more elaborate. For example, instead of this:



Issue infractions with messages like this:


Thoughts?

replies.author: StaticFaultz
replies.body:
@MLG: I understand that my example may appear to be much more complicated, but a bit of elaboration does go some ways to change how an infraction is taken.

@Howsie: I just edited the punishment page with Inspect Element; it's just a few fake images. Language/Caps shouldn't be heavily elaborated on, yes, I agree with that, but stating an infraction a much more direct way would change how it is taken. Writing up ones' infraction in a much more direct, human-like manner (like "Don't talk in caps") has much more "intensity" or "effect" than a more robotic, automated-seeming message ("Language/Caps").

@Tigor: That is not what I stated in the OP. Re-read. I am being an advocate for making more elaborate messages in this thread; not an assailant.

@Ingigo: That's great.

@SnowSX3: Of course. I think our examples are a little bit more elaborate than what would suffice, but that is better. Perhaps making it appear like the player is "talking" to the player in the punishment would improve it though. "Don't use caps! You've been warned."
